config.theme: Go/no-go for the Aurora mobile app launch
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Go/no-go for the Aurora mobile app launch

personas.name: Margot
personas.goals: A launch that works for every patron, including the oldest
personas.hidden_agenda: The library board wants the app live before the budget hearing

personas.name: Elliot
personas.hidden_agenda: His contract renewal depends on a smooth launch

personas.name: Fatou
personas.goals: The app works with screen readers and for people new to smartphones
personas.hidden_agenda: Runs a weekly phone-skills class for seniors and knows what confuses them

personas.name: Stan
personas.goals: No surprises for the help desk
personas.hidden_agenda: The login system is old and he worries about it

agenda.title: Beta results
agenda.goal: Review how patrons used the beta

agenda.title: Branch readiness
agenda.goal: Make sure every branch can support the app

beats.summary: Stability, login and screen readers; Elliot's login figure is challenged and corrected
Readiness across the system; Margot's branch count is off and stays off

turns.speaker: Margot
turns.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Let's start with the beta. Elliot, what did patrons actually do with it?

turns.speaker: Elliot
turns.text: About nineteen hundred patrons used the beta over six weeks. The most popular thing by far was holds. They placed sixty-four hundred holds through the app.

turns.speaker: Fatou
turns.text: That matches what I hear at the desk. People love not having to call.

turns.speaker: Stan
turns.text: The phone line has been quieter, actually. I noticed that before I knew why.

turns.speaker: Margot
turns.text: And e-books?

turns.speaker: Elliot
turns.text: Thirty-one fifty checkouts. Fewer than holds, but growing every week.

turns.speaker: Fatou
turns.text: Some of the older patrons didn't know e-books were free. The app is the first time they've seen them.

turns.speaker: Margot
turns.text: That's lovely to hear. That's the whole point of the thing.

turns.speaker: Stan
turns.text: Did people use the barcode on the phone instead of the plastic card?

turns.speaker: Elliot
turns.text: More than we expected. At the main branch the self-checkout machines read it fine.

turns.speaker: Fatou
turns.text: At the smaller branches the scanners are older. A few struggled with phone screens.

turns.speaker: Margot
turns.text: Which branches?

turns.speaker: Fatou
turns.text: Riverside and the bookmobile, mostly. Bright screens confuse the old scanners.

turns.speaker: Stan
turns.text: Those scanners are on the replacement list. Next year, I think.

turns.speaker: Fatou
turns.text: Should we hold the launch at those two until the scanners are replaced?

turns.speaker: Margot
turns.text: Then for now we tell patrons at those two to bring the plastic card as well.

turns.speaker: Fatou
turns.text: I'll put a note in the app's help section about the older scanners.

turns.speaker: Margot
turns.text: Quality. How stable is it?

turns.speaker: Elliot
turns.text: Crash-free sessions were ninety-nine point seven percent. Our target is ninety-nine five.

turns.speaker: Stan
turns.text: So we're above the bar. Good.

turns.speaker: Elliot
turns.text: And login failures are down to about half a percent.

turns.speaker: Stan
turns.text: Hmm. I'm not sure about that. The help desk log felt worse than half a percent. More like one in a hundred.

turns.speaker: Elliot
turns.text: You might be right. Let me look properly. Yes, it's one point four. Half a percent was iOS on its own.

turns.speaker: Margot
turns.text: One point four percent of people can't log in. That's a lot of frustrated patrons.

turns.speaker: Stan
turns.text: Most of it is people who've forgotten their PIN. The old system makes resetting it painful.

turns.speaker: Fatou
turns.text: In my class, half the questions are about PINs. People write them on the back of the card.

turns.speaker: Margot
turns.text: Can the app make resetting a PIN easier?

turns.speaker: Elliot
turns.text: It can link straight to the reset page. That's a small change.

turns.speaker: Stan
turns.text: The reset page itself is the problem. It's from two thousand eleven.

turns.speaker: Margot
turns.text: Let's do the link now, and look at replacing the reset page after launch.

turns.speaker: Elliot
turns.text: I'll add the reset link this week.

turns.speaker: Fatou
turns.text: Screen readers. There are still two issues open.

turns.speaker: Margot
turns.text: Are they serious?

turns.speaker: Fatou
turns.text: One is. The hold confirmation isn't announced, so a blind patron doesn't know if the hold worked.

turns.speaker: Elliot
turns.text: That one we can fix before launch. The other is a label on the settings page.

turns.speaker: Fatou
turns.text: Both, ideally. It's not much.

turns.speaker: Elliot
turns.text: Both, then. They're small.

turns.speaker: Margot
turns.text: And general bugs?

turns.speaker: Elliot
turns.text: Eight open. None of them stop anyone doing anything.

turns.speaker: Margot
turns.text: Branches. We have fifteen branches, and every one needs to be able to help a patron with the app.

turns.speaker: Stan
turns.text: Sixty-four staff have done the training so far.

turns.speaker: Fatou
turns.text: Mostly from the bigger branches. The small ones have one or two people on shift.

turns.speaker: Margot
turns.text: How do we cover the small ones?

turns.speaker: Fatou
turns.text: A one-page guide at every desk, with screenshots. People can follow it even if they haven't done the training.

turns.speaker: Stan
turns.text: And the help desk number on the bottom, for anything harder.

turns.speaker: Margot
turns.text: I like that. A one-page guide at every desk, then.

turns.speaker: Fatou
turns.text: I'll design it and get it printed before launch.

turns.speaker: Stan
turns.text: My daughter just started at the community college, by the way. She says their library app is terrible.

turns.speaker: Elliot
turns.text: Most university library apps are terrible. They're built by committees.

turns.speaker: Fatou
turns.text: Ours is built by a committee too, if we're honest.

turns.speaker: Margot
turns.text: Well, a careful committee. Let's get back to it.

turns.speaker: Stan
turns.text: The help desk needs to know the launch date before anything goes public.

turns.speaker: Elliot
turns.text: It'd be good if someone wrote up the five questions the help desk will get most.

turns.speaker: Stan
turns.text: I can do that. I already know what they'll be.

turns.speaker: Margot
turns.text: So. Are we ready for September ninth?

turns.speaker: Elliot
turns.text: From the development side, yes, with the reset link and the two screen-reader fixes.

turns.speaker: Fatou
turns.text: Yes, if the hold confirmation is announced. That's the one I care about.

turns.speaker: Stan
turns.text: Yes. The help desk will be ready.

turns.speaker: Margot
turns.text: Then it's a go for September ninth, with those fixes in.

turns.speaker: Fatou
turns.text: Will we tell all forty-eight thousand card holders at once, or start smaller?

turns.speaker: Margot
turns.text: An email to everyone, but we start the promotion at the branches the week before.

turns.speaker: Stan
turns.text: Has anyone asked the board whether they want a launch event?

turns.speaker: Elliot
turns.text: I'll send the final build to the app stores on the second, so there's time for review.

turns.speaker: Margot
turns.text: Thank you, all. This has been a careful piece of work.
